variants.specifics: Brackenford: Garrick at the north gate, shut by Halvard while Red Corwin's bandits rob the north road.

first.speaker: Garrick
first.text: Halvard, look here, it's one more fool who wants to try the north road past Red Corwin's bandits!

again.speaker: Garrick
again.text: Not much traffic through this gate lately.

later.speaker: Garrick
later.text: Wanna walk the north road, now that Corwin's gone?

variants.specifics: Varrhold: Brask guards the gate of the Great Lift, shut by Mayor Haldrek while the Undead hold the Deep; later the Mayor orders it opened for the player.

again.speaker: Brask
again.text: Back away from the lift, lad! Unless you WANT a ride down to the dead!

later.speaker: Brask
later.text:
Hold it right there, stranger! Mayor Haldrek orders the Great Lift opened for you, and his seal on this paper says so.

Step in! I've got a cold and rattly cage all set to drop you.

Will you go down quietly, stranger?

variants.specifics: Skeel: Grell guards the landing gate of Skeel and sends visitors to Warden Hobbe.

first.speaker: Grell
first.text: I'd speak to Warden Hobbe first... unless you'd like a swim with the leeches.

again.speaker: Grell
again.text: Hey, you ought to find yourself some proper boots.

later.speaker: Grell
later.text: Dead men on the ladders! Stand aside, stranger!

variants.specifics: Gorst: Brunk keeps the east gate, shut until Lord Dravus gives his word to open it.

first.speaker: Brunk
first.text: Only sworn soldiers may pass this gate!

again.speaker: Brunk
again.text: What are you still standing here for? Lord Dravus is holding court in the Great Hall right now! You'd better see him if you hope to pass this gate. His word opens it.

variants.specifics: Ombry: Brosk at the causeway gate, shut by Mayor Varrow while Gurlok's Ogres hold the Lamp Tower on Gull Isle.

first.speaker: Brosk
first.text: Fancy gear, stranger. But that buys you no passage over the causeway! Now back to the village with you!

again.speaker: Brosk
again.text: Back to the docks, stranger! Mind the nets!

later.speaker: Brosk
later.text: Hold it right there, Adventurer! Mayor Varrow says you threw the Ogres off Gull Isle and the light in the Lamp Tower proves it! Off you go. I've got the causeway gate open and waiting just for you! Will you be needing a boat too, Adventurer?

variants.specifics: Merinth: Brannock keeps the College gate, shut while Zorvan's Golems roam the streets.

first.speaker: Brannock
first.text: You want into the College with Golems loose in the streets!? You're mad! Now go away! You're a menace!

later.speaker: Brannock
later.text: So you're the hero of Merinth now! The College gate is open to you! As its keeper, I have seen many a famous face pass through. I'm sure you'll be the finest of them.

variants.specifics: Fort Vosk: Holm, the guard at the Frostgate, frightened of the frozen dead coming down the pass.

first.speaker: Holm
first.text: I can feel a dark shadow creeping over the pass! Will any of us live to see the spring?

again.speaker: Holm
again.text: We must hold the Frostgate and honor the men who fell up in the pass today!

later.speaker: Holm
later.text: Zombies! Ugh! I know what those creatures do to soldiers! Stay back!

variants.specifics: Durgal: Brannock keeps the north gate, shut by Guildmaster Krell since Bargul's Ogres took the Smelting Pits.

first.speaker: Brannock
first.text: Whoa! Nobody's going out that gate!

later.speaker: Brannock
later.text: The north gate is open, but you must report to Guildmaster Krell at the Great Forge when you return. May your luck hold out in the Smelting Pits, Wanderer!

variants.specifics: Pellor's Cross: Ruddock keeps the north gate of Pellor's Cross while Bludgor's Ogres hold Gallows Hill.

first.speaker: Ruddock
first.text: I'm afraid old Tobbe has gone soft in the head. They've put me on the north gate since he took to wearing a soup pot on his head and saluting the crows.

again.speaker: Ruddock
again.text: Well, well! You look a good deal tougher than the last hero they sent us! Come by the gate for a mug of cider when you're done with the Ogres.

later.speaker: Ruddock
later.text: The Ogres of Gallows Hill were a filthy and greedy pack of brutes! The worst was their lord, Bludgor!

variants.writer: Claude Agent SDK general-purpose agent, Claude Opus 5.5

variants.specifics: Vellin: Kestrin, the guard at the north gate, whose own barley the Ogres trampled.

again.speaker: Kestrin
again.text: Phewwwww! Keep that Ogre stink away from me!

later.speaker: Kestrin
later.text: Oh, you again. Are the Ogres gone, yet?
